To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we provide a fast randomized algorithm to approximate the statistical leverage scores of a kernel matrix that can be used to construct fast and statistically efficient sketches for kernel ridge regression, and we provide an empirical study showing that these sketches are useful in practice.

(i) we identify a notion of statistical leverage for kernel ridge regression, which is the number of columns needed in the sketch; (ii) we provide a fast algorithm to approximate these leverage scores; and (iii) the running time of our sketching algorithm is linear in the sample size and independent of the size of the kernel matrix.
we provide an efficient algorithm for computing a fast randomized sketch of kernel matrices that comes with running-time guarantees, as well as improved statistical guarantees.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of speeding up the running time of a kernel method while preserving its statistical performance, and our results show that this can be achieved with improved running times and improved statistical performance.
the following question: How can we use a small sketch of a kernel matrix to solve a kernel regression problem, while retaining statistical guarantees?
the design of efficient randomized algorithms for kernel methods that are both fast and provably accurate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is the best of both worlds: it has the statistical guarantees of the leverage score based approach, and the computational efficiency of the sketch based approach.
our approach provides a new and improved way to perform kernel ridge regression in a fast and provably statistically efficient manner.
we provide a new algorithm for kernel ridge regression that is faster than the previous best algorithms, and that also comes with better statistical guarantees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a fast randomized algorithm that comes with improved statistical guarantees for a large class of machine learning tasks.
we provide a new approach for fast randomized algorithms for statistical learning problems with provable guarantees.
, for a given data set, we can identify the important data points, compute their kernel values, and build a fast sketch of the input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of statistical learning problems, one should not only care about the size of the input but also about its \emph{structure}, which we capture by the concept of statistical leverage.
, in kernel-based learning, one should sample the columns of the feature matrix, not the rows.
the statistical leverage scores can be used in a principled way to reduce the computational cost of kernel-based methods.
